subject.title: Write tool lacks append mode — isolated cron sessions destroy shared files

question: Should OpenClaw standardize the fix as `append: true` on the existing `write` tool, a separate `append` tool, or another model-facing file-write contract?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the durable fix changes a public tool contract and the active PR already carries compatibility/session-state merge-risk labels, so automation should not choose the API shape on its own.

options.title: Approve append on `write`
options.body: Use the active linked PR direction, require it to rebase cleanly, and verify host and sandbox append behavior before merge.

options.title: Prefer a dedicated append tool
options.body: Ask the linked PR to rework the API so append and overwrite remain separate model-facing operations.

options.title: Defer tool API change
options.body: Keep prompt/backups/workarounds for now, accepting that ordinary agent and cron writes can still clobber shared files.

recommendation.title: Approve append on `write`
recommendation.body: Use the active linked PR direction, require it to rebase cleanly, and verify host and sandbox append behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans the agent runtime/tool boundary and long-term product contract, and `steipete` is the strongest history signal for that area.
